A +16.9pp gap on the Argentina side. Argentina v Austria in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Argentina stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Elo numbers going in: Argentina 2140, Austria 1830. That's a 310-point lead for Argentina — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Argentina to win at 76%, the draw at 11%, and Austria to win at 13%. The home side reads 76% on this distribution — the model's central case for Argentina.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Argentina to win at 59%, the draw at 24%, and Austria to win at 18%. Polymarket has Argentina at 59%, which prices out at American odds of −144; the model has the same side at 76%. The +16.9pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Argentina the lower bound is 66%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +7.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 34 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Argentina a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +16.9pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: Argentina are favourites on the market at 59% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 76%, a +16.9pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
